main_text.head: SUBSECTIO TERTIA. De Refrænatione fastuosi OEconomi, Sibi domum ædificantis.
Analysis.
main_text.p: §. 1. P[?]roponitur hic alia comminatio, judicium exponens, adversus fastuosum quendam Occonomum decretum; qui ex prædicatis nobis eruendus venit. Haud equidem dubitandum amplius existimo, quin, qui hic ut reus, & divinitùs judicandus repræsentatur, in eorum classe & numero sit recensendus, qui se regno Christi opponerent, seu quorum anima non foret recta in Christum. Verum, cum adversantium alii sint hostes ecclesiæ Christianæ publici, alii sub specie credentium obvelati: qui hic depingitur sub formâ œconomi, sibi domum fabricantis, & ex injusto quæstu ad operis istius promotionem maximas sibi opes facultatesque conquirentis; sanè concipi debet adversarius secundæ classis; à fastu, quem commonstrat, culpandus, aliisque criminibus eum consequentibus condemnandus.

§. 2. Sermo, qui de pessimo illo consultatore habetur, est Dei, oraculum suum continuantis; & consilium fastuosi condemnantis; licet illud aliàs sapientiæ carnali videri possit consilium hominis prudentis, & conservationem authoritatis ecclesiæ promoventis. Absolvitur verò duplici alloquio.
I. Alloquium ad prophetam, denunciationem judicii exhibet, quod huic imminebat. vers. 9. ubi.

page.notes: The drop-cap initial is ornamented and hard to read; I read it as P, so the first word is marked [?]. The "§. 1." and "§. 2." marks sit at the left edge of the text block and were treated as margin notes. "N." and "Ju-" at the foot right were read as the signature and catchword; the placement is uncertain. The running head was given with its chapter and verse reference, since those words are printed above the text. "Occonomum", "fastuosum" and the Analysis heading were read as italic from the scan. Long s is written as plain s throughout.
